version.changelog: v5.3.1 — agent mailbox rental is $15/mo (was $10/mo); nothing else changed.

llm.summary: The skill clearly provides a remote postal-mail service for agents, and its sensitive capabilities are disclosed with sandbox, cost, and human-approval safeguards.

dimensions.detail: Remote API calls, bearer tokens, document uploads, mailbox search, and webhook configuration are proportionate to a postal-mail API; the artifacts do not show local file indexing, local credential scraping, destructive local commands, or unrelated data collection.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Most integration paths use a hosted remote MCP server with bearer authentication; the README and install guide also include unpinned npx-based setup/bridge examples, which are common but should be installed from a trusted source.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill grants agents sensitive mail workflows, including sending physical letters and reading inbound mail/OCR, but it repeatedly scopes those actions through API keys, dry runs, cost caps, MAILBOX.md version checks, and human approval for inbound scan/forward/discard proposals.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill can configure webhooks and relies on persistent remote account state such as mailboxes, credits, standing instructions, and inbound mail records, but this is disclosed and aligned with the service; no local persistence, backdoor, or privilege escalation behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The advertised purpose is sending and managing physical mail through mailbox.bot, and the REST/MCP examples match that purpose: outbound mail, inbound OCR search, mailbox actions, webhooks, and billing status.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to let an agent interact with mailbox.bot. Use sandbox keys first, keep API keys out of prompts/logs, prefer agent-scoped keys with the minimum scopes needed, review dry-run prices before live sends, and require human approval for sensitive mail, legal notices, forwarding, scans, or discard actions.
llm.findings:
[TM1] expected: The flagged DELETE endpoint is a documented cancellation operation for already-submitted outbound mail, limited to the submitted state and tied to refund behavior; it is not evidence of unsafe tool-parameter abuse in this artifact.
[RP1] expected: The unpinned npx install/bridge examples create ordinary supply-chain caution for users, but the artifact is primarily a remote MCP integration and does not include local executable payloads.
[RP1] expected: The README's npx skill install line is an installation convenience rather than hidden runtime behavior; users should verify the publisher/source before installing.
[E1] expected: The external curl examples send requests to mailbox.bot using the user's API key to read mailbox data, which is the core purpose of the skill and is explicitly documented.
[SQP-2] expected: The install guide discloses a remote MCP server and sensitive mail capabilities, though a more prominent privacy and retention warning would improve user understanding.
[SQP-2] expected: The Smithery manifest advertises mail, document, webhook, and mailbox capabilities but is terse; the fuller SKILL and README provide the relevant operational safeguards.
